title: Equality & Diversity
blurb: The nine protected characteristics, direct and indirect discrimination, and how to welcome every guest and colleague fairly.
siteNotes: Who handles reasonable adjustment requests from guests, and what the venue can offer (for example large-print or read-aloud menus, step-free tables)
Where staff report discrimination, and who to go to if the concern involves a manager
The venue's equality and diversity policy and where staff can read it
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-26. The nine protected characteristics, direct and indirect discrimination, and reasonable adjustments: Equality Act 2010 (sections 4 to 19 and 20 to 21). Assistance dogs are covered by the duty to make reasonable adjustments.

CHECK: the trainer's definition of indirect discrimination ("a rule or practice that unfairly disadvantages a particular group") is simplified. In law it is a provision, criterion or practice that puts people sharing a protected characteristic at a particular disadvantage, and that the employer or provider cannot justify. Confirm the simplified wording is acceptable for staff.
The list: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation. Matches the trainer.

cards.title: Equality & Diversity
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- name the nine protected characteristics
- explain direct and indirect discrimination
- welcome every guest and challenge discrimination

cards.title: A mixed team, mixed guests
cards.body: A great hospitality team is a mix of all sorts of people, and our guests are just as varied. Equality and diversity is about treating everyone fairly and valuing those differences, among the team and towards every guest. It is the right thing to do, and it is also the law.

cards.title: Nine protected characteristics
cards.body: The Equality Act 2010 protects nine "protected characteristics". Discrimination against someone because of any of these is unlawful.

cards.title: Direct and indirect
cards.body: Discrimination can be direct or indirect.

left.title: Direct
items: Treating someone worse because of who they are

right.title: Indirect
items: A rule or practice that unfairly disadvantages a particular group

cards.title: Welcome everyone, fairly
cards.body: It means welcoming all guests equally and making reasonable adjustments. It means recruiting and rostering fairly, and never letting a guest's or colleague's background affect the service or respect they get.

cards.title: Do not let it slide
cards.body: If you see discrimination or hear a comment that crosses the line, challenge it if it is safe to, or report it. Diversity makes us a better, richer team and a more welcoming venue.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Nine protected characteristics, and discrimination on any of them is unlawful.
- Direct is treating someone worse because of who they are. Indirect is a rule or practice that unfairly disadvantages a group.
- Make reasonable adjustments and welcome assistance dogs.
- Never let someone's background change the service or respect they get.
- Challenge it if safe, or report it. Never let it slide.

cards.q: How many protected characteristics does the Equality Act protect?
cards.why: The Equality Act 2010 protects nine protected characteristics.

cards.q: Discrimination can be direct or indirect.
cards.why: Direct means treating someone worse because of who they are. Indirect means a rule or practice that unfairly disadvantages a group.

cards.q: Which of these is a protected characteristic under the Equality Act?
cards.why: Religion or belief is one of the nine. Age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, sex and sexual orientation are the others.

cards.q: We should make reasonable adjustments so all guests are welcome.
cards.why: Examples are reading a menu aloud, welcoming an assistance dog or finding an accessible table.

cards.q: A guest arrives with an assistance dog. You should…
options: Ask them to leave the dog outside
Ask for proof of training first
cards.why: Welcome them without fuss. This is one of the reasonable adjustments we make.

cards.q: A guest's background should be allowed to affect the service they receive.
cards.why: Never let a guest's or colleague's background affect the service or respect they get.

options: Treating someone worse because of who they are
A guest complaining about an unfair price
A rule or practice that unfairly disadvantages a particular group
Refusing a request that breaks the venue rules
cards.why: Indirect discrimination is a rule or practice that unfairly disadvantages a particular group. Treating someone worse because of who they are is direct.

cards.q: If you hear a discriminatory comment, you should just let it slide.
cards.why: Do not let it slide. Challenge it if it is safe to, or report it.
Diversity makes us a better, richer team and a more welcoming venue.

cards.q: Treating everyone fairly and with respect is both right and the law.
cards.why: It is the right thing to do, and it is also the law under the Equality Act 2010.
